heading: EXT. HOT-AIR BALLOON LAUNCH FIELD - BEFORE DAWN

units.text: EXT. HOT-AIR BALLOON LAUNCH FIELD - BEFORE DAWN
A cold meadow under a lavender sky.
Dozens of balloons lie limp on the dew, fans roaring, burners flaring orange against the dark.
JUNO ASHFORD, thirties, a pilot in a quilted vest, checks the basket's rigging.
COLM BRADY, thirties, her ground chief, holds the crown line.
PHOEBE LINWOOD, thirties, a journalist, stands at the basket with a notebook, her scarf wrapped twice.
Okay, everyone, burners on in two minutes.
units.name: JUNO

units.text: Colm nods.
He glances at Phoebe, then at Juno, then back at Phoebe.
She smiles.
He looks away fast.
Is it always this cold?
units.name: PHOEBE

units.text: Always. That's how you know it'll be worth it.
units.name: JUNO

units.text: She takes Phoebe's hand and helps her over the wicker rim.
Colm watches this with an expression he hides.
He busies himself with a knot.
Idiot. Idiot. Idiot.
units.name: COLM

units.text: What was that?
units.name: JUNO

units.text: Nothing! Rigging.
units.name: COLM

units.text: The burner roars.
The envelope swells.
Phoebe steps back, awed, and bumps into Juno, and neither of them moves away.
Colm drops the line, picks it up, drops it again.
Is anyone else coming up?
units.name: PHOEBE

units.text: I'll hold the ground.
units.name: COLM

units.text: Colm. Come up.
units.name: JUNO

units.text: He hesitates.
She reaches down a hand.
He takes it.
She hauls him over the rim, and the three of them stand shoulder to shoulder in the basket as the balloon lifts, silent, into the first pink light.
